findings.state: Capability row 03 mock card 'At risk' (scroll to capabilities)
findings.problem: Declarative certainty (dimension 4). The mock product screen states a forecast as fact; the live Future Autopsy deliberately renders 'If nothing changes, {name} is at {risk} risk of stalling or being lost within the next {days} days' (src/future-autopsy/v4/FutureAutopsyV4.tsx:145/187), part of the owner-approved evolution that avoids forecast certainty. The landing page re-asserts the certainty the app removed and does not use a string the app renders.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §13 (product demos behave like real software), §21 (claims discipline); owner-approved evolution 'Future Autopsy generation that avoids false causation and forecast certainty' (ANTAEUS_FINAL_AUDIT_CONTROL_PACKET_2026-11-16/antaeus-audit-control/01_OWNER_REQUIREMENTS.md, Approved product evolution)
findings.proposed: Cobalt Freight · $84k · high risk of stalling within 9 days

findings.current: Deals at risk, flagged early. Antaeus flags a deal before it stalls and recommends the smallest next step to keep it moving.
findings.problem: Certainty: 'flags a deal before it stalls' asserts a prediction the product only estimates (risk score from record staleness, stage age, missing next step). Paired with the 'stalls in 9 days' mock it tells a first-time buyer the product forecasts stall dates.
findings.proposed: Deals at risk, flagged early. Antaeus scores each open deal for stall risk from its record (days since update, stage age, missing next step) and recommends the smallest next step to keep it moving.

findings.state: Hero ranking demo (row 'Harbor Point' signal) and weekly routine Thu card (line 289)
findings.current: {nm:'Harbor Point', sg:'no buyer activity · 21d', ...}  /  Thu: 'Follow up on deals with no recent buyer activity.'
findings.problem: Claims discipline. The product does not measure buyer activity on deals; it measures days since the deal record was updated, and the app itself says so ('The deal record was last updated N days ago; this is not a measure of buyer activity', src/future-autopsy/lib/causes.ts:105). The mock claims a measurement the app explicitly disclaims.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §21 ('If the product knows only that there has been no logged activity, say that'), §13
findings.proposed: sg:'no logged activity · 21d'  and Thu: 'Follow up on deals with no logged activity.'

findings.current: A new General Counsel search or a newly hired CFO is detected, scored, and ranked against your target customer profile. You don't have to enter these events yourself.
findings.problem: Overstates automation. Account signals arrive when the operator runs enrichment (Signal Console 'Enrich' button → src/signal-console/lib/enrich-actions.ts runEnrichAll, POST /enrich against a configured enrichment server) — they are not detected continuously in the background. 'You don't have to enter these events yourself' is true only after the user triggers enrichment.
findings.proposed: When you run enrichment on an account, Antaeus pulls public company events — a new General Counsel search, a newly hired CFO — scores them, and orders accounts by priority against your target customer profile. You don't type these events in yourself.

findings.current: Raised off the line = at risk. One deal is on track. The rest are at risk, and you can't tell which one is about to stall.
findings.problem: Private visual metaphor (the lifted Living Mark) explained by an '=' sign — punctuation carries the logical relation (COPY_STANDARD §18) and the reader must learn the mark's grounded/lifted code to read the illustration.

findings.proposed: Each tilted mark is a deal at risk; the one standing on the line is on track. You can't tell which at-risk deal is about to stall.

findings.current: Signup takes a few minutes. Onboarding helps you define your first ICP and sets up your first ranked Dashboard. By the end of setup you're not browsing features — you're already using Antaeus.
findings.problem: Contradicts the shipped onboarding. The seeding flow (canon §4.3, ADR-019) deliberately asks for real work — ICP interview, account list, at least 10 live deals with judgment, quota — and its doorway says so. Telling a visitor setup takes 'a few minutes' and only defines an ICP misleads them about the effort and what is collected.
findings.governing: COPY_STANDARD.md §21; CLAUDE.md §4.3 Onboarding (heavy-seeding doctrine — never apologize for or hide the work)
findings.proposed: Signup takes a few minutes. Setup asks for real information — your ICP, the accounts you're targeting, and at least ten live deals — and uses it to build your first Dashboard, in order of what needs attention first. By the end of setup you're already using Antaeus.

findings.current: A time-limited event suggesting an account may be ready to buy. Ranked by account priority, source, recency, and ICP match, and shown as a ranked list of accounts to act on, not a passive timeline.
findings.problem: ICP match is not an input to the ordering: Signal Console orders accounts with rankByHeat (src/signal-console/v4/lib/attention.ts:144) and heat = signal count × type weight × source credibility × recency (src/signal-console/lib/heat.ts:11). ICP match is shown only on the older account cards. Also 'Ranked by account priority' is circular (priority is the ranking). Repeating 'ranked' twice compresses.
findings.proposed: A time-limited event suggesting an account may be ready to buy. Signal Console orders accounts by priority — how many signals each has, what kind, how credible the source is and how recent — so you see which account to act on first, not a passive timeline.
